- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.50), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is trending down.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply “cool-down” correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day for 3–5 days post-spike.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70–72), model tends to hold or overreact; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until reversion completes.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 0.5–1.0% for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., +0.5, -0.3, +0.8), model may misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction for next 3–5 days.
